This petition is filed under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, seeking to quash the proceedings against the petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 5 in C.C.No.251/2025, arising out of Crime No.152/2024, registered by Turvihal Police Station, pending on the file of Civil Judge and JMFC at Maski, for the offences punishable under Sections 85, 115(2), 329(4), 352, 351(2), 351(3),
54 r/w Section 190 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 [for brevity, the 'BNS, 2023'] and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 [for brevity, 'the D.P. Act'].
2. The factual matrix of the case is that, petitioner No.1 - Mallappa married respondent No.2 on 24.12.2021.
At the time of marriage, the parents of respondent No.2 gave Rs.75,000/- cash along with 3 tolas of gold and household articles to the petitioners.
After the marriage, respondent No.2 joined the matrimonial home and the petitioners looked after her properly for a period of one year.
Thereafter accused No.1 addicted to bad vices and NC: 2026:KHC-K:1007 HC-KAR used to harass respondent No.2 both physically and mentally by demanding additional dowry of Rs.3,00,000/-.

Though the said aspect was informed by respondent No.2 to accused Nos.2 and 3, i.e., the in-laws,
they instead advising their son-accused No.1, instigated him and abused respondent No.2 and also harassed her mentally.
Later, they all thrown her out from the matrimonial home.
As such, she started to reside at her parental house.

Things stood thus, on 21.11.2024 at about 5:30 p.m. accused Nos.1 to 5 trespassed the parental home of respondent No.2 and picked up quarrel with respondent No.2 by demanding Rs.3,00,000/- dowry and assaulted her.
As such, she lodged the complaint before respondent No.1 - Police on 28.11.2024 against the petitioners.

The same was registered in Crime No.152/2024 dated 28.11.2024 for the offences punishable under Sections 85, 329(4), 115(2),
133, 74, 54, 352, 351(2), 351(3) r/w Section 190 of BNS, 2023 and Sections 3 and 4 of D.P. Act.
Subsequently, respondent No.1 - Police investigated NC: 2026:KHC-K:1007 HC-KAR the case and laid charge sheet against five accused persons i.e., the petitioners.
Accordingly, learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offences.
Aggrieved by the same, the petitioners are before this Court.

3. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 and learned counsel for respondent No.2.
4.
Learned counsel for the petitioners, by reiterating the grounds urged in the petition, prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 and learned High Court Government Pleader opposed the petition and pray to dismiss the petition.

3 6.
I have given my anxious consideration both on the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties and the documents made available on record.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:1007 HC-KAR 7.
As could be gathered from records, the relationship between petitioners and respondent No.2 is not in dispute.
On perusal of the complaint averments, it is stated by respondent No.2 that, at the time of marriage, her parents had given cash of Rs.75,000/-, 3 tolas gold along with household articles.
Thereafter, though she was residing cordially in the matrimonial home for a period of one year, later her husband started to harass her both physically and mentally for additional dowry.
The petitioner Nos.2 and 3/accused Nos.2 and 3 are residing along with petitioner No.1/accused No.1.

On perusal of the complaint and charge sheet material, there are prima facie allegations forthcoming against accused Nos.1 to 3.
8.

However, insofar as petitioner Nos.4 and 5/accused Nos.4 and 5 are concerned, only allegation against them is that, after respondent No.2 left the matrimonial home, when she was residing at her parental house, on 21.11.2024 they all trespassed their house and assaulted her.
Except that, no other allegation is NC: 2026:KHC-K:1007 HC-KAR forthcoming against petitioner Nos.4 and 5/accused Nos.4 and 5.

Admittedly, petitioner No.4 is residing separately at Mailapur Road,
Turvihal Town, Sindhanur.

Petitioner No.5 is residing at Hirenandihall village, Kustagi Taluk,
Raichur.
In such circumstance, in my considered opinion, there is prima facie case made out against petitioner Nos.1 to 3/accused Nos.1 to 3 and proceedings against them cannot be quashed.

However,
as against petitioner Nos.4 and 5/accused Nos.4 and 5 are concerned, except some omnibus allegations, no other materials are forthcoming against them in the charge sheet.

9. In such circumstances, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of K. Subba Rao vs. State of Telangana represented by its Secretary, Department of Home and Others reported in 2024 INSC 960, at paragraph No.6 held that the Court should be careful in proceeding against the distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.

entities.text: K. Subba Rao vs. State of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Secretary, Department of Home and Others reported in 2024 INSC 960
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relatives of the husband should not be roped-in on the basis of NC: 2026:KHC-K:1007 HC-KAR omnibus allegations unless specific instance of their involvement in the crime are made out.

It is also settled position of law that if a person is made to face a criminal trial on some general and sweeping allegations without bringing on record any specific instances of criminal conduct, it is nothing but abuse of process of the Court.

The Courts pose a duty to subject the allegation levelled in the complaint to a thorough scrutiny to find out, whether there is any gain of truth in the allegations or whether they are made only with the sole object of involving certain individuals in a criminal charge, more particularly when a prosecution arise from a matrimonial dispute.

10. Further, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Dara Lakshmi Narayan vs. State of Telangana reported in 2025 3 SCC 735, held in para Nos.25 and 28 as under:
"25.

entities.text: Dara Lakshmi Narayan vs. State of Telangana reported in 2025 3 SCC 735
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A mere reference to the names of family members in a criminal case arising out of a matrimonial dispute, without specific allegations indicating their active involvement should be nipped in the bud.

It is a well-recognised fact, borne out of Mallappa @ Maleshi vs The State on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153229924/
4 NC: 2026:KHC-K:1007 HC-KAR judicial experience, that there is often a tendency to implicate all the members of the husband's family when domestic disputes arise out of a matrimonial discord.

entities.text: Mallappa @ Maleshi vs The State on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such generalised and sweeping accusations unsupported by concrete evidence or particularized allegations cannot form the basis for criminal prosecution.
Courts must exercise caution in such cases to prevent misuse of legal provisions and the legal process and avoid unnecessary harassment of innocent family members.

In the present case, appellant Nos.2 to 6, who are the members of the family of appellant No.1 have been living in different cities and have not resided in the matrimonial house of appellant No.1 and respondent No.2 herein.

Hence, they cannot be dragged into criminal prosecution and the same would be an abuse of the process of the law in the absence of specific allegations made against each of them.
28.
The inclusion of Section 498A of the IPC by way of an amendment was intended to curb cruelty inflicted on a woman by her husband and his family, ensuring swift intervention by the State.

However, in recent years, as there have been a notable rise in matrimonial disputes across the country, accompanied by growing discord and tension within the institution of marriage, consequently, there has been a growing tendency to misuse provisions like Section 498A of the IPC as a tool for unleashing personal vendetta against the husband and his family by a wife.

Making vague and generalised allegations during matrimonial conflicts, if not scrutinized, will lead to the misuse of legal processes and an encouragement for use of arm twisting tactics by a wife and/or her family.

Sometimes, recourse is taken to invoke Section 498A of the IPC against the - 10 - NC: 2026:KHC-K:1007 HC-KAR husband and his family in order to seek compliance with the unreasonable demands of a wife.

Consequently, this Court has, time and again, cautioned against prosecuting the husband and his family in the absence of a clear prima facie case against them."
11.

Applying the above findings of the judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court to the facts and circumstances of this case, continuation of proceedings against petitioner Nos.4 and 5/accused Nos.4 and 5 is abuse of process of Court.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a.
The petition is allowed in part.
b. The petition in respect of petitioner Nos.1 to 3 is dismissed and the proceedings against them shall continue.
c. The petition in respect of petitioner Nos.4 and 5 is allowed.

d. The proceedings against petitioner Nos.4 Mallappa @ Maleshi vs The State on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153229924/
5  and 5/accused Nos.4 and 5 in  C.C.No.251/2025, arising out of Crime No.152/2024, registered by Turvihal Police - 11 - NC: 2026:KHC-K:1007 HC-KAR Station, pending on the file of Civil Judge and JMFC at Maski, for the offences punishable under Sections 85, 115(2), 329(4), 352, 351(2),
351(3), 54 r/w Section 190 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, is hereby quashed.

Sd/-
